title: Three-Way Partition Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and two integers `low` and `high` (`low <= high`), partition the linked list into three consecutive sections:
1. All nodes with `val < low`
2. All nodes with `low <= val <= high`
3. All nodes with `val > high`

Preserve the **original relative order** of nodes within each of the three sections. Return the head of the partitioned linked list in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Create three sentinel dummy heads (`lessDummy`, `midDummy`, `highDummy`) and three corresponding tail pointers.

Route each node to its bucket in a single pass, terminate `highTail.next = null`, then connect `midTail.next = highDummy.next` and `lessTail.next = midDummy.next` (in that order, so empty buckets collapse automatically).

examples.explanation: All nodes fall in the middle range [0, 10], so the list stays [7, 3, 9, 1].
